subject: maths
title: Statistics Adventure 2: Tables & Diagrams
welcome_lead: Now you'll calculate averages from frequency tables, find the median in long lists, and read a stem-and-leaf diagram.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Statistics — mean from frequency tables, modal class, median position, and stem-and-leaf diagrams.
final_note: You can now find the mean from a frequency table, pick the modal class, locate the median in any list, and read stem-and-leaf diagrams.

concepts.def: How many times a value or class appears
Grouped class with the highest frequency
Diagram showing data sorted by tens and units
Tells you how to read the stems and leaves

walkthroughs.body_html:
When data comes in a table, use this formula:

Mean = Σ(value × frequency) ÷ Σ frequency

Add a column for value × frequency. Total it. Then divide by the total frequency.

For grouped data, use the midpoint of each class as the value.

The modal class is simply the group with the largest frequency. You don't pick a single value — just the class.

To find the median in a long list of n values, use:

Median position = (n + 1) ÷ 2

If n is even you'll land between two values — take their mean.

A stem-and-leaf diagram sorts data tidily. The stem is the tens digit, the leaf is the units digit.

Always check the key, e.g. "3 | 4 means 34".

Stem-and-leaf keeps every original value, so you can read off the median and range easily.

numericals.q: A frequency table shows: value 1 with frequency 2, value 2 with frequency 5, value 3 with frequency 3. What is the mean? (Answer to 1 decimal place.)

free_texts.q: For the ordered list 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, what is the median? Number only.
free_texts.hint: Six values — take the mean of the 3rd and 4th.
